In [[mathematics]], the '''Morrey–Campanato spaces''' (named after [[Charles B. Morrey, Jr.]] and [[Sergio Campanato]]) <math>L^{\lambda, p}(\Omega)</math> are [[Banach spaces]] which extend the notion of functions of [[bounded mean oscillation]], describing situations where the oscillation of the function in a ball is proportional to some power of the [[radius]] other than the dimension. They are used in the theory of [[Elliptic operator|elliptic partial differential equations]], since for certain values of <math>\lambda</math>, elements of the space <math>L^{\lambda,p}(\Omega)</math> are [[Hölder condition|Hölder continuous]] functions over the domain <math>\Omega</math>.

The [[seminorm]] of the Morrey spaces is given by 
:<math>\bigl([u]_{\lambda,p}\bigr)^p = \sup_{0 < r< \operatorname{diam} (\Omega), x_0 \in \Omega} \frac{1}{r^\lambda} \int_{B_r(x_0) \cap \Omega} | u(y) |^p dy. </math>
When <math>\lambda = 0</math>, the Morrey space is the same as the usual <math>L^p</math> space. When <math>\lambda = n</math>, the spatial dimension, the Morrey space is equivalent to <math>L^\infty</math>, due to the [[Lebesgue differentiation theorem]]. When <math>\lambda > n</math>, the space contains only the 0 function.

Note that this is a norm for <math> p \geq 1 </math>.

The seminorm of the Campanato space is given by
:<math>\bigl([u]_{\lambda,p}\bigr)^p = \sup_{0 < r< \operatorname{diam} (\Omega), x_0 \in \Omega} \frac{1}{r^\lambda} \int_{B_r(x_0) \cap \Omega} | u(y) - u_{r,x_0} |^p dy </math>
where 
:<math>u_{r,x_0} = \frac{1}{|B_r(x_0)\cap \Omega|} \int_{B_r(x_0)\cap \Omega} u(y) dy.</math> 
It is known that the Morrey spaces with <math>0 \leq \lambda < n</math> are equivalent to the Campanato spaces with the same value of <math>\lambda</math> when <math>\Omega</math> is a sufficiently regular domain, that is to say, when there is a constant ''A'' such that <math>|\Omega \cap B_r(x_0)| > A r^n </math> for every <math>x_0 \in \Omega</math> and <math>r < \operatorname{diam}(\Omega)</math>.

When <math>n=\lambda</math>, the Campanato space is the space of functions of [[bounded mean oscillation]]. When <math>n < \lambda \leq n+p</math>, the Campanato space is the space of Hölder continuous functions <math>C^\alpha(\Omega)</math> with <math>\alpha = \frac{\lambda - n}{p}</math>. For <math>\lambda > n+p</math>, the space contains only constant functions.
